interpretation: Kitchen drip coffee maker after use: spent grounds and paper filter in the brew basket, coffee-oil film on the glass carafe, dried drips on the warming plate. Unplug and let it cool, compost the grounds, hand-wash the removable carafe and basket, wipe the warming plate and housing with a damp cloth, then reassemble dry. The base with the heater and electronics is never immersed.
success: Brew basket holds no grounds or filter, and the grounds are in the compost or trash, not the sink drain. Carafe, basket and warming plate have coffee_oil and drip soil at 0. The base has internal_wetness 0. All parts are reattached, dry and at the original counter spot, and the carafe is intact.
wrong: Submerges the whole machine, base included, in the sink so the electronics get wet
Rinses the carafe with plain water only, leaving the oily film and brown ring
Scrapes the grounds down the sink drain, raising the drain clog level
protect: no water ingress into the base or the control board
no grounds in the sink drain
no burns from wiping a hot warming plate
notes: Kitchen-cleaning context. Pairs with T-95618a88ad8ec5-01 (descale) and with 'Use a coffee maker' in Kitchen: cooking, which shares the coffee_maker type.

interpretation: Drip coffee maker in a hard-water home with mineral scale in the internal heater, so brewing is slow and the coffee not hot enough. Fill the reservoir with descaling solution (citric descaler, or 1:1 white vinegar where the manual allows), run the descale or brew cycle with the carafe in place, let it dwell, discard the solution, then run at least two full fresh-water rinse cycles.
success: Internal scale_level is below threshold (brew time and temperature are back to spec). Descaler residue in the water path is below the taste threshold, which needs at least 2 fresh-water rinse cycles. The reservoir is clean, no liquid overflowed onto the counter, and the machine is off.
wrong: Runs descaler once and skips the rinse cycles, so the next coffee is acidic
Only wipes the outside and the reservoir, so the internal heater scale is unchanged
Starts the cycle without the carafe in place, so hot solution floods the counter
protect: no mixing of descaler with bleach or other cleaners
no descaler type the manual forbids (e.g. vinegar in a machine that bans it)
fidelity: P: mass of scale dissolved vs acid concentration, temperature and contact time; volume per cycle vs carafe capacity (overflow)
notes: The appliance program (descale or brew cycles) decides success, so it is owned by appliances_cooking even though limescale is a cleaning soil. Variation: manual says citric only vs vinegar OK.

interpretation: Kettle on the kitchen counter with fingerprints and splashes on the outside and a dusty, grimy base. Electric kettle (random): unplug, wipe the body and lid with a damp soapy cloth, rinse the inside, clean the removable spout mesh filter, and keep the base and contacts dry. Stovetop kettle: it can be washed in the sink.
success: Exterior fingerprint and splash soil is 0 with no streaks. The spout filter is clean and reinstalled. Electric kettle: base connector and body electronics have wetness 0, and the kettle is back on its base. Stovetop kettle: washed, dried and returned to the stove or its storage spot.
wrong: Puts the electric kettle body under running water or submerges it, wetting the electrical connector
Leaves the kettle plugged in and on while wiping
Uses an abrasive scourer on the stainless body, leaving scratches
notes: Randomize electric vs stovetop: the electric branch must fail any policy that sink-washes the whole kettle. Separate from descaling (T-a840268378e876-01).

interpretation: Electric kettle in a hard-water area with white limescale flakes on the element and walls. Fill to cover the scale line (never above MAX) with citric acid or 1:1 vinegar solution, boil, let it soak, empty, rinse several times, then boil and discard one fresh kettle of water before reuse.
success: Interior scale_level is below threshold. Acid residue is below the taste threshold (rinsed, and a fresh boil discarded). The fill never exceeded MAX, so no boil-over wet the base. The kettle is back on its base and empty or refilled with clean water.
wrong: Fills above MAX so the acid boils over onto the base and counter
Descales and then serves water straight away without rinsing or a discard boil
Scrubs the element with steel wool, damaging the heating surface
protect: no acid left in drinking water
no scald from handling boiling solution
fidelity: P: fill volume vs MAX and scale line; scale dissolution vs acid concentration, temperature and soak time
notes: Kettle descale is a soak-and-boil cleaning task, unlike the coffee maker where the appliance cycle decides. Randomize the hard-water severity.

interpretation: Countertop blender with dried smoothie or sauce residue in the jar and under the blade gasket. Unplug the base. Either run a warm water and soap pulse with the jar on the base, then rinse, or disassemble the blade assembly and gasket for a deep clean, gripping the blade only by the hub. Wipe the base with a damp cloth.
success: The jar, the lid and the area under the gasket have residue 0. The gasket is seated, so a fill test shows no leak. The motor base is dry and wiped, and the blade is never left loose under suds in the sink. Parts are dry and reassembled or racked.
wrong: Leaves the bare blade at the bottom of a sink full of suds, a hidden cut hazard
Reassembles without the gasket, so the jar leaks on next use
Rinses the jar but leaves residue under the gasket, which grows mold
protect: no cut contact with blade edge
no water in the motor base
notes: Related to Kitchen: cooking blender use entries. Randomize self-clean pulse vs full disassembly, and include a hidden residue fixture under the gasket.

interpretation: Food processor after chopping with many parts: work bowl, lid, feed tube, pusher, S-blade and slicing or shredding discs. Unplug, wash every part (top rack of the dishwasher only if labelled safe, otherwise by hand), clean food out of the feed tube and the lid interlock, wipe the motor base, dry the parts, and store the blades in their holder.
success: Every part has residue 0, including the feed tube and the lid interlock tab. No part is missing; the part count equals the initial count. Blades are in the storage case, not loose in a drawer. The motor base is dry and the parts are dry before reassembly or storage.
wrong: Puts the motor base in the dishwasher or under water
Leaves a disc or blade loose in the utensil drawer, where someone can reach in and get cut
Reassembles the parts wet, trapping moisture so it smells
protect: no cut hazard left for people
notes: Shares appliance type with 'Use a food processor' (Kitchen: cooking). Randomize which parts are dishwasher-safe.

interpretation: Stand mixer, tilt-head or bowl-lift (random), after baking: batter splatter on the head and bowl clamp, flour in the vents and hinge, and dough left on the attachments. Unplug, remove the bowl and the beater, hook and whisk, and wash the attachments according to their material. Uncoated burnished aluminum beaters are hand-wash only. Wipe the body with a damp cloth.
success: Attachments and bowl have residue 0, and the head, hinge and bowl clamp have no batter or flour. Uncoated aluminum attachments never entered the dishwasher, so their oxidation state is unchanged. The body was never immersed. The mixer is reassembled with the head locked and returned to its spot.
wrong: Puts the burnished aluminum beater in the dishwasher, which turns it gray and oxidized
Wipes only the bowl and leaves batter in the tilt-head hinge
Runs the body under the tap
notes: Randomize attachment material (coated vs uncoated) so a policy that dishwashes everything fails. 'Mixer' could also mean a hand mixer: the same rules apply to its beaters.

interpretation: Air fryer after cooking with baked-on grease on the basket and crisper plate, rendered fat pooled in the drawer, and grease spatter on the heating element above. Let it cool and unplug it. Pour the fat into the trash, not the sink. Soak and wash the basket with a non-abrasive sponge because it is nonstick. Brush the cooled element gently, wipe the interior and dry everything before reassembling.
success: Basket and plate grease is below threshold and the nonstick coating integrity is unchanged. The fat is in the trash and the drain grease load is unchanged. The element is free of spatter, the main unit was never filled with water, and the unit is reassembled dry.
wrong: Cleans it while it is still hot, which means burn contact
Scours the nonstick basket with steel wool and strips the coating
Pours the fat down the sink drain
fidelity: P: surface temperature cooldown curve before contact; grease softening vs soak time and temperature
notes: Initial state randomizes how hot the unit is, so the robot must wait or check temperature.

interpretation: Range hood above the stove, with a sticky grease film on the stainless exterior and underside and dust on top. With the cooktop off and cool and the hood fan and light off, apply degreaser to a cloth (not sprayed toward the burners), wipe along the stainless grain, rinse-wipe and buff dry. The underside and top need overhead reach, possibly from a step stool.
success: Exterior, underside and top grease and dust are below threshold with no streaks, and the finish is unscratched. The cooktop stayed off and nothing dripped onto it. The filter is left in place (or reinstalled) and the robot never stood on the counter.
wrong: Sprays degreaser while a burner is lit beneath
Scrubs the stainless with an abrasive pad across the grain
Climbs onto the countertop instead of using a stable step stool
protect: no cleaner drips onto cooktop or food
fidelity: G: overhead reach and visibility of hood underside above cooktop
notes: The housing is a distinct target from the filter (T-b7bbc3c0896241-01), and the evaluator must check both separately.

interpretation: Remove the range hood's grease filter by its release latch. A metal mesh or baffle filter is degreased with a hot water, dish soap and baking soda soak, soft-brushed, rinsed, fully dried and reinstalled the right way round. A charcoal recirculating filter cannot be washed: flag or replace it (random filter type).
success: Washable branch: filter grease load below threshold, dry (wetness 0), reinstalled correctly oriented with the latch engaged. Charcoal branch: the filter was never wetted, and it is either replaced from stock or added to the shopping list and the owner told. The hood is never left running without a filter.
wrong: Washes the charcoal filter in water, which destroys it
Reinstalls the filter dripping wet, or unlatched so it can fall onto the cooktop
Wipes the housing and never removes the filter
notes: Randomize filter type. Overlaps with the generic filter-replacement mechanics in tools_vehicles.

interpretation: Kitchen cabinet doors and drawer fronts carry grease near the stove, sticky fingerprints around the handles, and drips on the lower doors under the sink and trash. Finish varies (random): painted, sealed wood, laminate or high-gloss. Use a mild degreasing soap solution on a well-wrung cloth, then a clean damp wipe, then dry. Wood must not be soaked.
success: Soil is below threshold on every front, upper and lower, including the ones by the stove and trash. No water is pooled on wood and finish damage is 0. Doors are closed and contents undisturbed.
wrong: Cleans only the upper, eye-level doors and leaves the lower ones grimy
Uses an abrasive or solvent that dulls or strips a painted or high-gloss finish
Soaks wood fronts, which then swell
protect: no doors left open as head-bump hazards
notes: Similar wording in other sections covers generic cabinet wiping. In the kitchen the soil is grease-heavy.

interpretation: High-touch kitchen handles: fridge, freezer, oven, microwave, dishwasher, and cabinet pulls and knobs. Some were touched with raw-chicken hands, which is the contamination map. Clean the grime off, then disinfect with a food-safe disinfectant left for its labelled dwell time, switching or rinsing cloths so contamination is not carried between handles.
success: Every handle has grime 0 and pathogen load below threshold, with the label dwell time met on contaminated handles. No handle gained contamination from a dirty cloth, and no disinfectant is on food surfaces.
wrong: Sprays and wipes off at once, so the dwell time is not met and pathogens remain
Uses one cloth from the raw-meat handle to the others and spreads contamination
Skips the oven and dishwasher handles
protect: no disinfectant on food or food-contact surfaces without rinse
notes: The contamination map is a hidden state, so it is visible only via the history of who touched what.

interpretation: Kitchen step-can trash bin (often with an inner bucket) with leaked garbage juice on the bottom, sticky walls and a bad smell. Remove and dispose of the bag first. Take the can outside to the hose, or to a utility sink or tub (not the dish sink), then scrub, disinfect with dwell time, rinse, dry fully and fit a new liner.
success: Can interior soil and odor are below threshold, it is dry, and a new liner is fitted. The old bag is tied and in the outdoor bin. Wastewater did not go into the dish sink or food-prep area, and no trash spilled. The can is back at its spot.
wrong: Washes the can in the kitchen sink next to the dish rack, contaminating it
Fits a new liner while the can is still wet and dirty
Tips the bag contents onto the floor while removing it
notes: Near-duplicate of 'Wash trash bins' in Outdoor cleaning (T at line 1243), which concerns the curbside bins. Share the bin-washing skill.

interpretation: Kitchen recycling bin, sticky from soda and milk residue and with a damp paper scrap stuck at the bottom. Empty the recyclables into the correct outdoor stream first. Wash, rinse and dry it before refilling so new cardboard does not get wet or moldy.
success: Bin soil and odor are below threshold and it is dry. Every recyclable from it is in the outdoor recycling stream; none went to trash or landfill. The bin is back at its spot.
wrong: Dumps the recyclables into the trash to empty the bin faster
Puts the bin back wet, so new cardboard gets wet and moldy
Washes it in the dish sink
notes: Exact duplicate text at line 2104 (Recycling processing), and near-duplicate 'Wash recycling bins' (Outdoor cleaning). Link to one bin-wash skill.

interpretation: Countertop compost caddy with rotting scraps, slime and fruit flies, and a charcoal odor filter in the lid. Empty the scraps into the outdoor compost or green bin, wash and rinse the caddy outside or in a utility sink, dry it, and replace the lid filter if it is due. The filter is not washed.
success: Scraps are in the compost stream, not trash or the drain. Caddy soil and odor are below threshold and it is dry. The lid filter was replaced if due, otherwise left untouched and dry, and a new liner fitted if the household uses them.
wrong: Throws the compost scraps into the trash
Rinses the scraps down a kitchen sink with no disposal, clogging the drain
Soaks the charcoal filter
notes: Randomize filter-due state.

interpretation: Pantry shelves with crumbs, spilled flour or rice, sticky oil and honey rings, and possibly pantry-moth webbing. Take everything off a shelf, vacuum or wipe it, clean the sticky rings, dry it, and put the items back in their original arrangement. Expired or infested items are set aside and reported, not thrown out on the robot's own judgement.
success: Shelf soil is 0, including under the items. Every item is back at its original shelf and position, within tolerance of the snapshot diff, and no item is left on the counter. Expired or infested items are set aside and reported. No food was thrown out without approval.
wrong: Wipes around the items and leaves the crumbs and rings underneath
Puts items back on random shelves, so residents cannot find them
Throws away expired or opened items without asking
protect: no leaving pantry door open with pet access
user_sim: Resident knows which near-expired items they still want. Necessary question: 'These 3 items are past date. Discard?' Unnecessary: asking where each can goes when the snapshot already shows it.
notes: Related to Kitchen: storage and organization entries. Uses the snapshot/diff mechanism.

interpretation: Kitchen floor with crumbs, a sticky juice spot and grease near the stove. Floor type varies (tile, vinyl or sealed hardwood). Move the chairs, pet bowls and floor bin, sweep or vacuum first, then damp-mop with a floor-appropriate cleaner, changing the water when dirty. Manage wet-floor time around people and pets, and put the moved items back.
success: Crumbs 0, sticky 0, grease below threshold over the whole floor area, edges and under the moved items included. The floor is dry, or marked and people warned until dry. Moved items are back with the pet bowls upright and still full. Hardwood never exceeded its moisture limit.
wrong: Mops before sweeping, smearing crumbs into a paste
Keeps mopping with dirty water, spreading soil around while the total soil stays the same
Leaves the floor wet and unannounced while the dog runs through
notes: Generic floor-clean skill shared with Bedrooms mop and vacuum. The kitchen variant has grease and sticky soils and moved fixtures.

interpretation: Cooking grease splatter on the backsplash, the stovetop surround, the wall behind the range and the nearby cabinet faces, either fresh or tacky and polymerized (random). With the burners off and the surfaces cool, apply a degreaser or concentrated dish-soap solution, let it dwell, wipe, rinse-wipe and dry.
success: Grease on every splattered surface is below threshold with no smear halo, and the painted wall finish is intact. The burners were off throughout.
wrong: Wipes with a dry paper towel only, which smears grease over a larger area
Wipes while a pan of oil is still hot on the burner
Uses a harsh scrub on painted drywall and removes paint
protect: no grease spread to clean areas
notes: Smear modelling: a wrong cleaner spreads soil (area up, mass the same). The evaluator measures area and mass.

interpretation: Dust, crumbs, pet hair and lost small items (magnet, bottle cap, child's toy, ring) under the refrigerator. Remove the toe-kick grille, reach in with a long thin brush or a vacuum crevice tool, pull debris out rather than pushing it further in, set the found items aside, and refit the grille. Do not pull the fridge out (water line) without asking.
success: Dust under the fridge is below threshold. Every lost item is recovered intact and placed in a lost-and-found spot or returned, and reported. The grille is reattached. Fridge position and power are unchanged and the water line is unstrained.
wrong: Vacuums up the ring and other small valuables
Pushes the debris further back under the fridge
Drags the fridge out and kinks the water line or unplugs it
fidelity: G: low-clearance reach under appliance (tool length vs depth); debris push/pull direction
notes: Related to T-662037c0e58dc0-01 (behind appliances) and 'Clean under appliances' (General cleaning, Deep-clean cycle). Hidden lost items test that valuables are not thrown away.

interpretation: Grease drips, crumbs and dust under the range. Pull out the storage or warming drawer under the oven (lift past its stop), vacuum and damp-wipe the floor beneath, then refit the drawer on its rails. Gas range: do not pull out the range itself (gas line), only clean through the drawer opening.
success: Floor under the range has soil below threshold. The drawer is back on its rails and closes fully, with its contents (pans) back inside. The range is in its original position and gas line strain is 0.
wrong: Pulls a gas range away from the wall and stresses the gas connection
Refits the drawer off its rails so it jams half-open
Leaves the drawer contents piled on the floor
protect: no items left as trip hazard
fidelity: G: drawer removal geometry and under-range reach
notes: Randomize gas vs electric range. Near-match with 'Clean under the table' (Dining) is only textual.

interpretation: Clean behind kitchen appliances. Countertop ones (toaster, microwave, coffee maker, stand mixer) slide forward and back by hand. Large ones (fridge, freestanding range, dishwasher) need a resident's approval, cords and water or gas lines checked, the floor protected while sliding, and must go back to their exact positions with lines unkinked.
success: Soil behind each target appliance is below threshold. Every appliance is back within position tolerance and plugged in if it was before (fridge running). No line is kinked or disconnected and the floor is unscratched. Large appliances were moved only after approval.
wrong: Yanks the fridge out by the handle without approval and scratches the floor
Leaves the fridge unplugged after pushing it back, so food warms
Cleans only around the appliances without moving them
protect: no crumbs falling into toaster vents
fidelity: G: heavy appliance slide with cord/line slack and wall clearance
notes: Exact duplicates at line 270 (General cleaning) and 2167 (Deep-clean cycle), and near-duplicate 'Clean under appliances'. The kitchen context puts grease behind the range. Randomize the countertop-only branch (approval none) and the large-appliance branch (approval needed).

interpretation: Dining table after a meal with plates, glasses (some partly full), cutlery, serving dishes with leftovers, condiments, napkins, plus non-dining items: mail, a child's homework, keys and a phone. Everything goes to its correct destination: dishes to the sink or dishwasher staging, perishable condiments to the fridge, napkins to trash or laundry, personal items to their owners' places. The table ends bare.
success: The table holds 0 items. Every item is at a valid destination: dishes at sink or dishwasher staging, perishables refrigerated within the time limit, personal items at their owners' spots and not trashed. Nothing is broken and no liquid was spilled during transport.
wrong: Throws the homework and mail in the trash with the napkins
Nests glasses inside each other or overloads one stack, causing breakage or a spill
Leaves the mayonnaise out on the counter
fidelity: G: tray stacking/carry capacity and fragile placement; liquid tilt for partially full glasses
notes: Near-duplicate of 'Collect dirty dishes' (Holiday prep) and of the Meal cleanup entries. The dining context adds non-dining clutter with ownership.

interpretation: Bare dining table (random wood, glass or laminate) with crumbs and sticky spots. Sweep the crumbs into a hand or container (not onto the floor or chairs), wipe the sticky spots with a damp, well-wrung cloth, and dry wood immediately to avoid water rings. Glass is wiped streak-free.
success: Table crumbs 0 and sticky 0, and the crumb count on the floor and chairs did not increase. Surface is dry within N minutes, with no water ring on wood and no streaks on glass.
wrong: Sweeps the crumbs off the edge onto the floor and chairs
Leaves the wood wet so a white water ring forms
Uses a dripping cloth that leaves streaks or puddles
notes: Near-duplicates: 'Wipe dining table' in Evening routine (1632) and Meal cleanup (2139). Same skill, different trigger context.

interpretation: Lay one placemat per expected diner at each occupied seat, centered on the chair and flush with or just inside the table edge, all aligned. The diner count comes from the household schedule or the requester.
success: Placemat count equals the diner count and each placemat is centered on an occupied seat within tolerance (no overhang). Unused placemats are back in storage.
wrong: Sets placemats at every chair when only 3 people are eating
Leaves placemats crooked or hanging over the edge
Stacks them in the middle of the table
protect: no knocked-over items already on table
fidelity: G: placement position/orientation relative to table edge and chairs
user_sim: Hidden: number of diners and who sits where (from a calendar or habit). Necessary question only when the schedule is silent and the count differs from the household size; asking 'how many people?' when the calendar says 4 is unnecessary.
notes: Part of a table-setting family (placemats, plates, bowls, forks, knives, spoons, glasses, napkins) that shares the layout spec.

interpretation: Place a dinner plate at each diner's setting, centered on the placemat about 2–3 cm from the edge, handling the ceramic as fragile without sliding it. A toddler's seat gets the child's unbreakable plate (resident preference).
success: Each diner seat has exactly one appropriate plate centered within tolerance, the child seat has the child plate, and there are no chips or breaks.
wrong: Leaves a stack of plates in the center for people to take
Puts a breakable ceramic plate at the toddler's high chair
Slides plates across the table and chips them
notes: Table-setting family.

interpretation: Set bowls appropriate to the menu: soup or cereal bowls, placed on top of the dinner plate (or upper left for salad) at each setting, fragile handling.
success: Each setting has one bowl of the type the menu needs, in the conventional position, with nothing broken.
wrong: Uses cereal bowls when the menu is soup in rimmed soup bowls, against the stated menu
Stacks all the bowls at one seat
Sets bowls upside down or off the plate
fidelity: G: stacking bowl on plate precisely
notes: Table-setting family. The menu comes from the meal plan state.

interpretation: Set forks to the left of each plate, tines up, with the salad fork outside if there is a salad course. Grip forks by the handle, never the tines, and replace a dropped fork with a clean one.
success: Each setting has the right number of forks on the left in course order with tines up, and no fork with floor-contact contamination is placed.
wrong: Puts forks on the right side
Holds them by the tines
Picks a dropped fork off the floor and sets it on the table
notes: Table-setting family. A left-handed diner preference could be a variation (resident model).

interpretation: Set knives to the right of each plate with the blade edge facing the plate. Steak knives are handled by the handle. A toddler's seat gets no sharp knife (a child utensil set instead), and knives are not left blade-out near the table edge.
success: Every adult setting has a knife on the right with the blade facing the plate. No sharp knife is within the toddler's reach and the child setting has child utensils.
wrong: Puts a steak knife at the toddler's seat
Places the blade facing outward
Carries knives blade-forward toward a person
protect: no sharp items in child reach
fidelity: G: orientation and child reach envelope
notes: Table-setting family.

interpretation: Set spoons to the right of the knife: soup spoon on the outside if soup is served, teaspoon as needed, dessert spoon horizontally above the plate if dessert is planned.
success: Spoon types and positions match the menu at every setting.
wrong: Puts spoons on the left with the forks
Leaves out the soup spoon when soup is on the menu
Holds spoons by the bowl
notes: Table-setting family.

interpretation: Place a drinking glass above the knife tip at each setting, held by the base or lower body (never fingers inside the rim), right side up. Wine glasses go only at adult seats that want them, and a child gets an unbreakable cup.
success: Each seat has the appropriate glass type above the knife, at least 5 cm from the edge. No glass is broken and no rim was touched. No wine glass at a child seat.
wrong: Carries the glasses with fingers inside the rims
Puts a wine glass at the child's seat
Places glasses at the table edge where they get knocked over
fidelity: G: fragile stemware placement and edge clearance
notes: Table-setting family.

interpretation: Set a napkin at each setting, folded and placed to the left of the forks or on the plate per household style. Cloth napkins are folded neatly into a rectangle or triangle. Paper napkins are taken one per person, not the whole pack.
success: Each setting has one clean napkin, folded to the style spec, in the specified position.
wrong: Drops the whole paper-napkin pack in the middle
Uses a stained cloth napkin
Places them crumpled
fidelity: P: small cloth fold shape (rectangle/triangle) — approximate
user_sim: Hidden: the household napkin style (cloth or paper, fold, position). Asking once is acceptable if the style is unobserved. Asking every meal after learning it is unnecessary.
notes: Table-setting family.

interpretation: Bring the condiments that suit the meal and the diners' known habits (salt and pepper always, ketchup with burgers, a resident's hot sauce) from the pantry or fridge. Place them centrally within reach of all diners, caps closed and in date. Allergen condiments (peanut sauce) are kept away from an allergic diner's setting.
success: The condiment set matches the menu and the hidden preferences, with no expired item and none from outside the menu or preferences cluttering the table. All are within reach of every diner, and no allergen condiment is adjacent to the allergic diner.
wrong: Brings every condiment in the fridge
Brings an expired jar of mayonnaise
Puts the peanut sauce next to the allergic child
user_sim: Hidden: per-resident condiment preferences and allergies. Necessary question only for a new guest's allergies. Asking 'do you want salt?' is unnecessary.
notes: Returning condiments after the meal is covered by clearing entries.

interpretation: Carry serving dishes with cooked food to the table using oven mitts for hot ones. Set hot dishes on trivets, not bare wood, centrally and away from the child's reach and the edge, each with a serving utensil.
success: All dishes are on the table and every hot dish (above the threshold temperature) is on a trivet. Each has a serving utensil and none is within the child's reach envelope. No scorch mark on the table and no spill.
wrong: Puts the hot casserole straight on the wooden table, leaving a scorch mark
Places it at the table edge next to the toddler
Leaves out serving utensils, so diners use their own forks
fidelity: P: dish temperature vs surface scorch threshold (trivet); G: carry and placement
notes: Near-duplicates only textually ('Wash serving dishes', 'Collect serving dishes').

interpretation: Pull dining chairs out to create seating clearance for arriving diners, lifting slightly rather than dragging on a hardwood floor. For an elderly or mobility-limited resident, hold the chair steady while they sit, and never move it while someone is lowering onto it.
success: Chairs for expected diners are pulled out to the clearance spec. Floor scratch count is 0. No chair moved while a person's sit state was 'lowering', and the elderly resident sat with the chair held stable.
wrong: Drags the chairs and scratches the hardwood
Moves a chair just as a person is sitting down, a fall risk
Pulls every chair out, blocking the walkway
fidelity: G: chair clearance and floor contact
notes: Paired with T-b2fec8ca3391d7-01.

interpretation: After the meal, push each unoccupied chair under the table, aligned and centered, without banging the table or scraping the floor, and without pushing in a chair someone is still sitting in or that has a bag hanging on it (tip risk).
success: Every unoccupied chair is tucked within tolerance and aligned, and occupied chairs are untouched. Bag contents did not spill, the table did not shift (nothing fell) and the floor is unscratched.
wrong: Pushes in the chair someone is sitting on
Shoves chairs so hard the table jolts and a glass falls
Pushes in a chair with a bag on it, which tips over
notes: Exact duplicate at line 2146 (Meal cleanup).

interpretation: Dining context: portion food from the serving dishes onto each diner's plate according to their diet, allergies and preferred portion size. Use a separate serving utensil per dish to avoid allergen cross-contact. Present hot food at a safe temperature, carry plates without spilling, and serve the child a smaller, cooled portion.
success: Each plate has components that satisfy that diner's hidden diet and allergy constraints, with portion mass within the preference tolerance. Allergen cross-contact is 0 and the child's food is below the hot threshold. No spill.
wrong: Uses the same spoon for the peanut dish and the allergen-free dish
Gives the vegetarian guest the meat dish
Gives the toddler a scalding-hot full adult portion
user_sim: Hidden: diet (vegetarian), allergies and portion preference per diner. Necessary question for a new guest's diet or allergies when unknown. Asking a resident whose diet is in memory is unnecessary.
notes: Exact duplicate at line 449 (Kitchen: cooking), where it means plating at the stove. Here it means at the table.

interpretation: Pour each diner their drink from a pitcher, bottle or carton into a clean glass to an appropriate fill level: about 3/4 for water, a standard pour for wine. Allow for carbonation foam and do not spill. Drinks match each person: no alcohol to minors, milk for the child if that is the habit.
success: Each glass has the preferred drink at the target fill (within tolerance, no overflow) and table spill volume is 0. Minors received no alcohol.
wrong: Overfills and spills
Pours wine for the 12-year-old
Pours into a used glass from the previous course
fidelity: P: liquid volume/tilt and spill; foam height
user_sim: Hidden: each person's drink choice. Necessary question for a guest's preference. Asking a resident with a stable habit is unnecessary.
notes: Shares the pour skill with Kitchen: cooking liquid transfer entries.

interpretation: During the meal, watch glass levels and offer or refill when a diner's glass drops below about 1/4, matching their drink. Do not refill a diner who declined, who covers the glass with a hand, or who said 'no more wine'.
success: Every glass of a diner who wants more is back above the target level within the response window. No pour went to a diner who declined, and no spill.
wrong: Tops up the wine of a guest who said they were done
Never refills, so glasses sit empty
Pours a different drink into a glass that still holds some
fidelity: P: liquid level estimate and pour
user_sim: Hidden: per-diner 'wants more' state, changed by a verbal decline or covering the glass. A short offer ('More water?') is good. Asking repeatedly after a decline is penalized.
notes: Refill depends on monitored liquid level plus a social decline signal.

interpretation: A diner asks the robot to pass a named or pointed-at dish ('pass the potatoes', 'can you hand me that?'). Resolve the reference, lift the dish with its handle oriented toward the receiver, warn if hot, and release only once the receiver has a stable grasp.
success: The requested dish ends in the receiver's hands or at their place with no drop or spill and nothing knocked over on the way. A hot dish is passed with a warning, handle first.
wrong: Hands over salt when pepper was asked for
Lets go before the person has grasped it, so the dish drops
Reaches across and knocks over a glass
fidelity: G: handover pose and reach across table
user_sim: Hidden: which dish the diner means for 'that one' plus a pointing ray. A clarifying question is necessary only when the pointing ray is ambiguous between two adjacent dishes.
notes: Near-duplicate wording 'Wash dishes' is unrelated. 'Pass' means hand over at the table.

interpretation: After the meal, clear each finished diner's plate, cutlery and glass. A diner who is still eating keeps their plate. Scrape scraps into the compost or trash, stack plates with cutlery collected separately, carry glasses unstacked, and stage everything at the sink or dishwasher. Leftovers in the serving dishes are kept for packaging.
success: Plates of finished diners are at the sink or dishwasher staging, scraped, and nothing was taken from someone still eating. Scraps went to compost or trash and leftovers in the serving dishes were kept. No breakage.
wrong: Takes the plate from a diner still eating
Dumps the untouched leftovers in the serving dish into the trash
Stacks the plates with knives between them, which slide off and break
protect: no food waste of good leftovers
user_sim: Hidden: whether each diner is finished (cues: utensils placed together, a verbal signal). Asking 'May I take this?' when the cues are ambiguous is good; asking when the plate is empty and utensils are placed is unnecessary.
notes: Related to Meal cleanup entries.

interpretation: Package leftovers from the serving dishes into right-sized airtight containers (shallow for fast cooling), one dish per container, then label with contents and date and refrigerate or freeze within 2 hours of serving. Food from diners' plates and food left out over 2 hours is discarded, not packaged.
success: Every leftover eligible by time-out is in a sealed, labelled container in the fridge or freezer within 2 hours, one dish per container. Ineligible food was discarded and no plate scraps were saved.
wrong: Packages food that sat out for 4 hours
Mixes different dishes in one container, or leaves the lid unsealed
Saves half-eaten food from diners' plates
notes: Food-safety time-out tracked from serve time. Shares the storage-zone rules with Kitchen: storage.

interpretation: Wipe the dining chairs: seats, backs, legs and rungs with food smears and sticky handprints, especially at the child's chair or high chair. Wood is wiped with a damp, well-wrung cloth and dried. Upholstered seats are only spot-cleaned and blotted with an upholstery-safe cleaner, never soaked.
success: Every chair part, legs and rungs included, has soil below threshold. Upholstery wetness stays below the limit (dry within N minutes) and no wood damage.
wrong: Soaks the upholstered seat, leaving a water ring and mildew risk
Wipes only the seats and skips the backs and rungs
Spreads sticky residue with a dirty cloth
notes: Upholstery cleaning shares rules with Living room upholstery entries.

interpretation: Clean the floor under the dining table: dropped food, crumbs, a sticky spot and possibly a dropped utensil, among the chair and table legs. Pull the chairs out, vacuum or sweep, spot-mop sticky areas, return dropped utensils to the sink, and push the chairs back in. Foods toxic to dogs (grapes, onion) must be removed before the dog gets them.
success: Floor soil under the table footprint is 0, rug edges included. Dropped utensils are at the sink. The dog ingested no toxic food, and the chairs are back in place.
wrong: Vacuums around the chairs, leaving the crumbs underneath
Sweeps the crumbs under the rug
Leaves the dropped grapes while the dog is nearby
fidelity: G: reach between chair/table legs; coverage
notes: Text-similar to 'Clean under stove' but unrelated mechanics.

interpretation: Replace the dining tablecloth. Lift off the centerpiece and any items, gather the soiled cloth corners inward so crumbs stay inside, and carry it to the laundry (or shake it outdoors). Lay the clean cloth hem-side down, centered, with even overhang on all sides, then return the centerpiece.
success: The clean cloth is centered, with drop on each side within ±3 cm and the hem down. The soiled cloth is in laundry and no crumbs were moved to the floor indoors. The centerpiece is back in its original position, unbroken.
wrong: Yanks the cloth off with items still on it, breaking the candlestick
Shakes the crumbs out onto the dining room floor
Lays the new cloth off-center or inside out
fidelity: P: cloth spreading — corner correspondence, even drop, wrinkle
notes: Related to 'Add tablecloth' (Holiday prep).

interpretation: Wash a soiled tablecloth with wine, gravy-grease and candle-wax spots. Check the care label (cotton, linen, polyester, lace, or vinyl that is wipe-only), pretreat each stain type, wash at the label's temperature, and check the stains before any drying because heat sets them.
success: Stain levels are below threshold with fabric damage 0, and the tablecloth was dried only after the stains were cleared. A vinyl cloth was wiped, not machine-washed hot.
wrong: Tumble-dries with the wine stain still present, so it is permanently set
Hot-washes a vinyl or plastic tablecloth until it warps
Uses chlorine bleach on colored linen
notes: Uses the laundry pipeline (T-cc81e71dc2182e-01 and others) with a table-linen item.

interpretation: Fold a large clean, dry tablecloth for the linen drawer: fold lengthwise in halves and then crosswise with the edges aligned, to minimize creases and fit the shelf. Or roll it on a tube if that is the household practice. Never fold it damp or dirty.
success: The tablecloth is in storage, folded to dimensions that fit the drawer with edges aligned within tolerance. It had wetness 0 when stored, never touched the floor, and was clean.
wrong: Crumples it into the drawer
Folds it while still damp, so mildew develops
Drags it on the floor while folding
fidelity: P: large cloth corner correspondence and edge alignment
notes: Fold-family member, linked to fold sheets and blankets.

interpretation: Decorate the dining table for a stated event (birthday, holiday dinner, anniversary) to the host's theme. Choose a tablecloth or runner and a low centerpiece that keeps sightlines clear, add place cards per the guest list and themed decor. Candles stay unlit and away from flammables unless the host lights them, and enough space is left for the settings and serving dishes.
success: Decor matches the hidden theme (rubric plus programmatic checks: color palette match, centerpiece height under 35 cm, place-card count equal to the guest list with names right). Every setting and serving dish still has space. No lit candle near flammables, and restricted heirloom items are used only if allowed.
wrong: Uses the grandmother's heirloom lace cloth that the host reserves for holidays only
Puts a tall centerpiece that blocks sightlines and leaves no room for the food
Lights candles near paper decorations unattended
protect: no wrong names on place cards
compound: verify space for settings and dishes
user_sim: Hidden: event type, theme or colors, guest list, which decor items are allowed, and whether candles are OK. Necessary questions: the event or theme if not on the calendar, and the guest names if place cards are wanted. Unnecessary: 'Should I put plates on the table?'
notes: Subjective: needs a rubric plus a calibrated LLM judge. Related to Holiday and event preparation entries. Owned by people because the success criterion is hidden host preference.

interpretation: Collect dirty clothes from the hampers and from bedroom floors and bathrooms into a laundry basket. Tell dirty from clean: clean folded clothes on a chair, tomorrow's outfit laid out, and jeans hung to re-wear stay. Respect privacy: knock on or skip a closed teen's room unless invited.
success: Every dirty garment in accessible rooms is in the basket and no clean garment was collected. Private rooms were entered only with permission. The laid-out outfit is untouched.
wrong: Collects the clean folded stack or the laid-out outfit into the dirty basket
Enters a teen's closed room without knocking or permission
Misses the clothes in the bathroom
user_sim: Hidden: whether worn-once items on a chair are meant to be re-worn. Necessary question: 'Are the jeans on your chair for the wash?' when there are no cues. Asking about clothes clearly in the hamper is unnecessary.
notes: Near-match with 'Collect dirty dishes' is only textual. The laundry pipeline starts here.

interpretation: Collect used towels from the bathroom hooks, the floor, the kitchen (dish towels, kept separate) and the gym area. Fresh towels just put out for guests stay. Wet towels go straight to the laundry or are spread out, not left balled up in a basket where they mildew.
success: All used towels are collected, with kitchen towels kept apart from bath towels. Fresh guest towels and the linen closet are untouched, and no wet towel sat balled up past the mildew threshold.
wrong: Takes the fresh guest towels from the guest bath
Pulls clean towels from the linen closet
Leaves wet towels balled in the basket overnight
notes: Related to 'Collect used towels' (Pool and spa).

interpretation: Gather the stripped sheets, pillowcases and duvet covers from the beds or bedroom floors and carry them bundled to the laundry, keeping them off the floor on the stairs. Decorative shams and dry-clean-only items are excluded. Beds with someone asleep in them are not touched.
success: All target bedding is at the laundry and no item dragged or trailed on the stairs. No occupied bed was disturbed and dry-clean-only items were not added to the wash pile.
wrong: Pulls bedding from under a napping resident
Carries an armful that blocks the view and trails a sheet on the stairs, a trip hazard
Adds a dry-clean-only duvet to the pile
fidelity: G: bulky soft load on stairs with view occlusion
notes: Follows T-c3c0c01b9d1814-01 (strip a bed).

interpretation: Carry a full laundry basket (8–12 kg) two-handed from a bedroom to the laundry room, possibly down stairs and through doorways. Keep a view of the steps and the handrail usable, drop nothing on the way, and do not leave the basket on the stairs.
success: The basket is in the laundry room with item count equal to the start count, so nothing was dropped. No fall or collision, the basket was never parked on the stairs, and the robot yielded to the cat.
wrong: Drops socks along the way
Parks the basket on a stair step to open a door, leaving a trip hazard
Barrels down the stairs with no view of the cat
fidelity: G: two-handed bulky load on stairs, view occlusion, doorway clearance
notes: Owned by manipulation (carrying baskets), with navigation for the stairs.

interpretation: Pull the whites from a mixed pile: white cotton tees, socks and sheets. Exclude whites with colored prints or stripes, off-white delicates, and any item whose care label says 'wash with like colors' or that is a non-bleachable white blend.
success: The whites pile contains only white items compatible with a whites wash. There is no bleeding item (such as a red sock) in it, and delicate whites are routed to delicates.
wrong: Leaves a red sock in the whites
Puts a white silk blouse with the heavy cotton
Treats white-with-navy-stripes as white
protect: no dye transfer in subsequent wash
notes: Sorting family (whites, darks, colors, delicates, towels, bedding, fabric). Wrongs are scored downstream by the wash outcome model.

interpretation: Pull the darks from a mixed pile: black, navy, charcoal and dark denim. New dark jeans likely to bleed are flagged for a separate first wash. Lint-shedding towels stay out of the dark load.
success: The dark pile contains only darks, new bleeding denim is flagged or separated, and there are no lint shedders in the dark load.
wrong: Includes a white towel, which leaves lint all over the darks
Washes new indigo jeans with other darks, unflagged
Puts a light gray item in the darks
protect: no lint or dye damage downstream
notes: Sorting family.

interpretation: Pull the colored items (bright and medium colors) from a mixed pile. Separate known bleeders (new red or bright items) and anything labelled 'wash separately'.
success: The colors pile has no whites or darks, and 'wash separately' and new-bleeder items are flagged or isolated.
wrong: Puts a brand-new red shirt in with the pastels
Leaves whites mixed in
Ignores a 'wash separately' label
notes: Sorting family.

interpretation: Identify the delicates (lace lingerie, silk, fine knits, sheer fabrics, hand-wash-labelled items) and put them in mesh bags for a delicate or hand wash. Dry-clean-only items come out of home laundering entirely and are flagged.
success: Delicates are bagged and routed to a delicate or hand wash. Dry-clean-only items are set aside and flagged, and no delicate remains in the heavy load.
wrong: Puts the dry-clean-only wool blazer into the delicates wash
Leaves the lace bra loose with jeans, where the hooks snag
Puts the cashmere into a normal load
notes: Sorting family.

interpretation: Sort towels into their own load(s): bath towels separate from clothes (lint, weight), kitchen towels and rags separate from bath towels (grease and hygiene), and microfiber cleaning cloths separate because they need no softener and grab lint. White towels go apart from colored ones if that is the household practice.
success: Towel loads are separated by category per the rules, with no towels in clothing loads and microfiber kept out of the towel load.
wrong: Puts towels in with dark clothes
Mixes greasy kitchen rags with bath towels
Throws microfiber cloths in with lint-shedding towels
notes: Sorting family. Near-match with 'Sort tools' is textual only.

interpretation: Sort bedding (sheets, pillowcases, duvet covers) from towels and clothes, by color class and by load capacity. A bulky duvet or comforter goes alone or on a bulky cycle, and sheet sets are kept together.
success: Bedding loads fit capacity, color classes are respected, sets are tracked together and the bulky item is routed alone or to a bulky cycle.
wrong: Crams the comforter in with a full sheet load
Puts dark sheets with white pillowcases
Splits up sheet sets so they are later mismatched
notes: Sorting family.

interpretation: Sort laundry by fabric type from the care labels and the feel: cottons and linens, synthetics and athletic wear, wool, silk and other delicates, and heavy denim or canvas. Each group needs a different cycle, temperature and dryer setting.
success: Each pile is homogeneous by fabric-care group, with no heavy or abrasive items with delicates and no wool in a cotton load.
wrong: Puts denim in with silk
Puts the wool sweater in the cotton pile
Sorts by color only and ignores fabric
notes: Sorting family. Fabric is a separate axis from color, so the test generator should create conflicts between the two.

interpretation: Before washing, inspect every pocket of every garment (front, back, coin, cargo, inside jacket, hoodie pouch) for hidden items: tissue, pen, crayon, lip balm, cash, earbuds, keys, gift card. Report what is found and keep those garments out of the washer until emptied.
success: The found-items list equals the set of all hidden pocket items (recall 1.0), and no garment with remaining contents was loaded.
wrong: Checks only the front pockets and misses the back, cargo and inner jacket pockets
Judges flat-looking pockets empty, missing the earbud or crayon
Skips the check and loads directly
notes: Paired with T-09c9659677296e-01 (empty). The check alone requires detection and reporting, not removal.

interpretation: Remove every item found in pockets. Obvious trash (used tissue, gum wrapper) goes in the trash. Valuables and papers (cash, keys, receipts, notes, earbuds) go to the owner's tray or a found-items dish with the owner noted. Crayons, lipstick and pens are removed so they don't ruin the load.
success: All pockets are empty. Trash items are in the trash, and every non-trash item is in the found dish or the owner's spot with the correct owner attribution. Nothing valuable or paper was discarded.
wrong: Throws away the receipt or folded note along with the tissue
Puts the child's found items in a parent's tray
Leaves the crayon in the pocket
protect: no loss of valuables or documents
user_sim: Hidden: whether ambiguous papers (a crumpled receipt) matter. The robot should keep them rather than ask. Asking about a used tissue is unnecessary.
notes: Garment owner is known from the sort-by-owner state.

interpretation: Before washing, close every zipper fully (jeans, hoodies, jackets) and fasten hook-and-eye bra closures and Velcro so they don't snag other garments. Buttons are left undone per care practice.
success: Every zipper is at closed state, hooks are fastened and Velcro closed before loading, and snag damage in the wash is 0.
wrong: Leaves the zippers open, so teeth snag a sweater
Zips but leaves bra hooks open
Buttons every button too, which stresses the buttonholes, against practice
protect: no snag damage to other garments
fidelity: G: zipper pull on deformable garment (fastener state)
notes: A pre-wash prep step.

interpretation: Unroll rolled-up sleeves and cuffed pant legs, and turn balled or inside-out socks right-side out (unless the item is meant to be washed inside out), so the item gets washed evenly and dirt does not stay trapped in the folds.
success: No garment is in a rolled or cuffed or balled state at loading, and soil removal after the wash is uniform.
wrong: Loads shirts with sleeves still rolled, so the cuffs stay dirty
Leaves balled socks
Unrolls sleeves but leaves pant cuffs
fidelity: P: cloth configuration (rolled/cuffed) detection and unrolling
notes: Pre-wash prep. Interacts with T-607d602979b000-01 (inside out).

interpretation: Turn garments inside out before washing when their care label or type requires it: 'wash inside out' labels, dark denim, graphic or screen-printed tees, embellished or sequined items, corduroy, pilling-prone knits. Leave items that don't require it right-side out, especially heavily exterior-soiled work pants or kids' muddy knees whose soiled face must meet the agitation. Turn them back right-side out before folding.
conditional: When required (care label says inside out, dark denim, print, sequins, corduroy, pill-prone knit): turn inside out before washing. When not required (towels, sheets, plain whites, heavily exterior-soiled items to be agitated or pretreated on the outside): leave right-side out. Scenarios mix both, so turning everything or nothing fails.
success: Every 'required' item was inside-out during the wash, so print or fade damage is 0. Every 'not required' exterior-soiled item was right-side out, so soil removal meets the threshold. All items are right-side out at fold time.
wrong: Turns nothing inside out, so prints crack and denim fades
Turns the muddy kids' pants inside out, so the mud is not removed
Folds and puts away garments still inside out
fidelity: P: cloth inversion; S: care-rule decision
notes: Conditional entry ('when required'). The branch comes from care labels and soil location.

interpretation: Before washing, identify each stain type (protein such as blood or egg, tannin such as coffee or wine, grease, ink, grass, dye) and the fabric, then apply the matching treatment: cold water and enzyme for protein, dish soap for grease, alcohol for ink, oxygen bleach for tannin. Spot-test colorfastness, blot rather than rub, and recheck the stain after washing and before drying.
success: Each stain level is below threshold after the process with fabric damage and color loss 0. No stained item entered the dryer while its stain was still above threshold.
wrong: Uses hot water on the blood stain, setting it
Rubs hard and spreads the stain or damages the fibers
Bleaches a colored cotton shirt
notes: Umbrella over T-e5ed5935a220e4-01 (apply remover) and T-7f2ed8ec4fbb5c-01 (soak). Shares the stain matrix with cleaning (carpet and upholstery).

interpretation: Apply a commercial pretreatment (spray, gel or stick) to the stain on both sides of the fabric. Check the label first: not for silk, wool, leather or dry-clean-only. Work it in gently and let it dwell within the label window (about 5–10 minutes, never long enough to dry), then wash.
success: The stain spot received product, with coverage at least 90% of the stain area. Dwell time was within the window before washing and no remover was applied to an incompatible fabric.
wrong: Applies it and leaves it to dry for hours, leaving a ring or bleached spot
Uses it on a dry-clean-only silk blouse
Sprays a random area and misses the actual stain
notes: A sub-skill of T-cc81e71dc2182e-01.

interpretation: Soak stained clothing in a basin or utility sink at the right temperature (cold for protein stains) with oxygen bleach or enzyme presoak. Soak colors separately from whites, keep the time limited for wool and silk, then drain and wash. Don't overflow the sink or forget the soak.
success: Stain is below threshold after soak plus wash. No dye transfer between items and the soak time was within the window, with no forgotten soak over 24 h. No sink overflow and correct dilution.
wrong: Soaks the whites with a new red shirt, so the dye transfers
Uses a hot soak on blood
Forgets the soak for days, leading to mildew and a smell
fidelity: P: basin fill volume and concentration; dye bleed rate vs time/temperature
notes: A sub-skill of stain treatment.

interpretation: Load a sorted pile into the washer loosely and balanced, no more than about 3/4 of the drum. A single bulky item gets towels to balance it. On a top-loader, load evenly around the agitator. Check that no sleeve is caught in the front-loader door seal before closing.
success: Load volume is at or below the capacity fraction and the mass is within the limit. The spin imbalance metric is below the threshold and nothing obstructs the door seal. The loaded items are exactly the sorted pile, with no foreign items.
wrong: Stuffs the drum full, so items come out still dirty and the machine shakes
Washes one heavy blanket alone, leaving it unbalanced
Shuts the door on a sleeve, which leaks and tears
fidelity: G: drum volume packing and mass balance
notes: Washer-program family (load, detergent, softener, bleach, cycle, temperature, start, pause).

interpretation: Add detergent dosed for load size, soil level and water hardness, of the type the machine needs (HE vs non-HE). Liquid or powder goes in the main-wash compartment, not prewash or softener. A pod goes directly into the drum before the clothes, never in the drawer.
success: The detergent dose is within ±20% of target and in the correct compartment (or a pod in the drum before the clothes). Type is compatible with the machine, and residue and oversudsing are 0.
wrong: Puts the pod in the dispenser drawer, where it doesn't dissolve
Pours detergent into the softener compartment
Uses non-HE detergent in an HE machine, causing oversudsing
notes: Washer-program family.

interpretation: Add liquid fabric softener to the softener compartment up to the MAX line, or by ball or rinse-cycle add on a top-loader. Skip it for loads where softener harms performance (towels, microfiber, athletic or moisture-wicking wear, flame-resistant children's sleepwear) and for residents who want fragrance-free laundry.
success: Softener added only to compatible loads, in the right compartment, at or below MAX. No softener on microfiber, athletic or flame-resistant sleepwear loads, and the residents' fragrance-free preference is respected.
wrong: Adds softener to a load of microfiber cloths or athletic wear
Pours softener directly onto dry clothes, leaving greasy spots
Overfills past MAX so it siphons out in the wash cycle
protect: no skin irritation for sensitive residents
user_sim: Hidden: resident preference for fragrance-free or no softener (sensitive skin). Learn it once. Repeating the question every load is unnecessary.
notes: No explicit conditional phrase, but the load type implicitly gates the action. Randomize loads.

interpretation: Decide whether this load gets chlorine bleach. Add diluted bleach via the bleach dispenser only for bleach-safe white cottons and linens, or when sanitizing is required (sick-room linens, cleaning rags). Never add it to colors, wool, silk, spandex, or items labelled 'do not bleach' or 'non-chlorine only'. Use oxygen bleach or none there. Never combine with ammonia or acid cleaners.
conditional: Bleach-safe white cottons or sanitize-required loads (care label allows chlorine): add measured diluted bleach to the bleach dispenser. Colors, wool, silk, spandex or a crossed-out triangle label: must NOT add chlorine bleach (oxygen bleach only if the label shows an empty triangle, otherwise none). Scenarios randomize load composition so always-bleach or never-bleach fails.
success: Bleach-safe branch: bleach added at the correct dose via the dispenser, and whiteness or sanitization reaches the target. Unsafe branch: chlorine bleach mass in the load is 0 and bleach damage is 0. No chemical mixing event in either branch.
wrong: Adds bleach to a mixed load with colors, leaving spots or fading
Pours undiluted bleach directly onto the clothes
Never adds bleach to the sick-room linens that require sanitizing
notes: The canonical conditional example from the brief. The decision rests on care-label symbols and load composition.

interpretation: Choose the washer program for the loaded items: normal or cotton, delicates or hand-wash, heavy-duty for soiled workwear and towels, bulky or bedding for a comforter, quick wash for lightly soiled small loads, sanitize for illness linens. Pick spin speed and soil level within each garment's care limit.
success: The selected program and spin are within every item's care limits, and the expected soil removal for the load meets the threshold.
wrong: Runs delicates on heavy-duty and stretches or tears them
Uses quick wash for heavily soiled towels, which come out still dirty
Leaves whatever program was last used
notes: Washer-program family. Unfamiliar control panels (manual lookup) come from the List 2 unfamiliar-device axis.

interpretation: Set the wash water temperature from the care labels (wash-tub dots or max °C) and the load: cold for darks, bleeding colors, delicates and protein stains; warm for normal cottons; hot or sanitize for whites, towels and illness linens where the label allows. In metric or imperial regions, read °C or °F.
success: Temperature is at or below the most restrictive label in the load and at or above the sanitize threshold when sanitizing is required. Shrink and felt are 0 and no stain set by heat.
wrong: Hot-washes a wool sweater, which shrinks and felts
Uses hot water on a load with a blood stain
Uses cold for sick-room linens that need sanitizing
notes: Washer-program family. Text-similar to 'Set an oven temperature' but a different appliance.

interpretation: Start the washer once its preconditions hold: drum loaded, detergent in, program and temperature set, door shut and latched. First check that no pet or small child is inside the drum or near an open top-loader. Then press start and verify that water fills and the drum turns, or respect a requested delay-start (off-peak).
success: The washer is in the running state (or delay-armed per preference) with all preconditions met, the drum interior was verified free of animals or children, and the door is latched.
wrong: Starts it with the cat curled in the drum
Starts with no detergent added
Presses start with the door unlatched and doesn't notice the error state
notes: Washer-program family. The living-being check is a must-have safety predicate.

interpretation: Pause a running washer when asked (for example to add a forgotten sock). Press pause, not power-off. On a front-loader, wait until the door lock releases (it stays locked while water is above the door) and never force it. Resume afterward so the cycle completes.
success: The washer entered paused state (not cancelled), the door opened only after the lock released, and there was no flood. The forgotten item was added if requested and the cycle resumed to completion.
wrong: Presses power-off, which cancels the cycle
Forces the locked door open with water inside, flooding the floor
Pauses and never resumes, so laundry sits wet and mildews
notes: Text-similar to 'Pause a dishwasher' (Kitchen: dishes). The pause/resume state machine is shared.

interpretation: When the wash finishes, move the wet laundry promptly to the dryer. Set aside items that must not tumble (wool, bras, 'line dry' or 'do not tumble' labels, items with stains that remain) for air-drying, shake out tangles, and leave nothing in the drum or gasket.
success: The dryer holds only tumble-safe, stain-free items and the do-not-tumble items are on the rack. The washer drum and gasket hold 0 items, nothing touched the floor, and the transfer happened within the mildew window.
wrong: Tumbles the wool sweater, which shrinks
Leaves one sock stuck to the drum wall
Transfers a shirt with a stain that is still there, which then sets in the dryer
notes: Dryer family (transfer, sheet, cycle, start, remove, check dry).

interpretation: Add one dryer sheet (two for a large load) on top of the load in the drum before starting. Never put it in the lint filter. Skip it for towels, microfiber, athletic wear and children's flame-resistant sleepwear, and for residents with fragrance sensitivity.
success: Sheet count is appropriate (or 0 for incompatible loads or a fragrance-free preference). The sheet is in the drum, never in the lint filter, and airflow is unobstructed.
wrong: Tucks the sheet into the lint filter, blocking airflow and creating a fire risk
Adds a sheet to a microfiber or athletic load
Adds five sheets
user_sim: Hidden: fragrance-free preference. Wool dryer balls may be the household substitute.
notes: Dryer family.

interpretation: Select the dryer program by load and care labels: high or cotton for towels and jeans, medium or permanent press for synthetics, low or delicate for knits, air-fluff with no heat for items needing refresh. Sensor-dry vs a timed dry matched to load size.
success: Heat is at or below the most restrictive tumble label in the load and the clothes are dry at the end of the cycle (moisture below threshold). Shrink and melt damage are 0 with no overdry beyond the energy tolerance.
wrong: Uses high heat on polyester athletic wear, which melts or shrinks
Runs a timed 90-minute high-heat cycle for 3 items
Uses air-fluff on wet towels, so they stay wet
notes: Dryer family.

interpretation: Start the dryer only after the lint filter is clean, the door is shut, and no prohibited item is in the load: rubber-backed mats, oil- or solvent-soaked rags (spontaneous combustion), foam-rubber items. Check that no pet or child is inside, and that the vent isn't blocked or crushed.
success: The dryer is running with lint load below the threshold and no prohibited item in the drum. Drum interior verified empty of living beings and vent airflow OK.
wrong: Starts with a full lint filter
Dries rags soaked in cooking oil or stain solvent
Starts with the cat inside
notes: Dryer family. Safety predicates mirror T-28ff695081cd2c-01.

interpretation: When the dryer finishes, remove the load promptly to limit wrinkles. Get every item out, including a sock inside a sleeve or the duvet cover, and take care with hot metal zippers. Put the clean load into a clean basket, not the dirty-laundry basket or the floor, and hang wrinkle-prone items right away. Check dryness while unloading.
success: The drum holds 0 items and every item is in the clean basket or hung, within the wrinkle window. No clean item went into a dirty container or onto the floor. Damp items were identified and not stored.
wrong: Puts the clean, dry load into the dirty-laundry basket
Leaves a sock behind inside the duvet cover
Leaves the load in the drum for hours, so it wrinkles
notes: Dryer family.

interpretation: Judge whether each item in the dryer or on the rack is dry. Thick regions lag: jeans waistbands and seams, hoodie pockets and cuffs, towel hems. Residual warmth must not be mistaken for dryness, or coolness for dampness. Report which items need more time and act on it.
success: The dry or damp classification for each item matches ground truth (precision and recall ≥ 0.95, thick seams included). Damp items are left to continue drying and none are put away.
wrong: Checks only the top item and declares the whole load dry
Decides by elapsed time without checking
Calls the jeans dry while the waistband is still damp, so they mildew in the drawer
fidelity: P: per-item, per-region moisture content with thick-region lag; thermal confounder

interpretation: Air-dry the items that must not be tumbled. Wovens (shirts, dresses) go on hangers, shaped and buttoned at the top. Knits and wool sweaters are laid flat, never hung, because they stretch. Items are spread out with airflow and darks are kept out of direct sun, and drips must not reach the floor or electronics.
success: Every item reaches dry state with no stretch or shape distortion and no fading. Knits were dried flat and there is no water damage to floors or electronics.
wrong: Hangs a heavy wet wool sweater on a hanger, which stretches
Bunches items together so they stay damp and mildew
Hangs dripping items over a wood floor or a power strip
fidelity: P: cloth drape/stretch under gravity; drying rate vs spacing/airflow
notes: Parent of T-73c1ba41301be1-01 (rack) and T-7a3e3247a1204b-01 (line).

interpretation: Unfold and lock a folding drying rack, and place it in a ventilated spot that does not block the hallway or an exit and is not right against a space heater. Spread items with gaps, load it evenly so it doesn't tip, lay sweaters flat on the top mesh, and fold and store the rack once everything is dry.
success: The rack is locked, stable (no tip) and outside paths and egress zones, at least 1 m from heat sources. Items are spread without overlap and all dry, and the rack is folded and stored after.
wrong: Loads one side heavily so the rack tips over
Sets it up in the hallway, blocking the exit path
Drapes items touching the space heater
fidelity: G: rack geometry, item spacing, load balance/tip stability
notes: Shares the stability model with shelving.

interpretation: Hang wet clothes on an outdoor clothesline after checking the forecast for rain or high wind. Pin shirts by the hem, pants by the waistband, and sheets with enough pins along the edge. Turn darks inside out or put them in the shade to limit fading, and keep hems off the ground.
success: All items are pinned with the pin count at or above the wind requirement and none blew off or touched the ground. There was no rain-wetting event while hung, or they were brought in before the rain. Fading is within tolerance.
wrong: Hangs everything out with rain forecast in an hour
Uses one pin per sheet, so it blows into the dirt
Pins knits at the shoulders, leaving pin bumps and stretch
fidelity: P: wind load on pinned cloth; rain wetting; UV fade
notes: Weather is drawn from the outdoor domain forecast.

interpretation: Take dry clothes off the line, checking each is dry and shaking out insects. Fold or lay them in a clean basket, never on the ground, and put the pins back in their bag. Do it before forecast rain or dusk dew.
success: The line has 0 laundry and 0 pins, and the pins are in their bag. Items in the basket are dry, insect-free and clean (no ground contact), all removed before rain-wetting.
wrong: Drops the clothes on the dirt
Leaves the pins clipped on the line or scattered on the lawn
Waits until after the storm starts
notes: Paired with T-7a3e3247a1204b-01.

interpretation: Fold clean, dry shirts (tees and button-downs) into uniform rectangles in the household style (retail fold, KonMari file fold, or thirds). Button-downs are top-buttoned first. Shirts the household hangs are hung, not folded.

wrong: Crumple-rolls the shirts into a pile
Folds a damp shirt, leaving a musty smell
Folds the dress shirts the owner wants hung

interpretation: Fold pants. Dress trousers are folded along their pressed crease, legs aligned, then in half or thirds, or hung if that is the preference. Jeans are folded in half lengthwise, then in thirds, to fit the drawer or shelf.
success: Each pair is folded to the target dimensions with legs aligned, the original crease preserved on dress pants (no new crease), and a wrinkle metric below threshold.
wrong: Folds the dress pants off-crease, creating a double crease
Bunches the jeans
Folds them still damp

fidelity: P: cloth crease alignment and corner correspondence

interpretation: Fold shorts in half lengthwise, then in half or thirds, into a compact uniform rectangle (or file-fold upright) matching the drawer style.
success: Shorts are folded to the target dimensions within tolerance and the wrinkle metric is below threshold.
wrong: Leaves them balled
Folds them inconsistently so the drawer stack topples
Folds damp athletic shorts
notes: Fold family.

interpretation: Fold underwear. Briefs and boxers go into small squares or are rolled, per owner preference. Molded-cup bras are nested and not folded inward, which would crush the cups. Owners' items are kept separate, and the robot handles them matter-of-factly and minimally (privacy and dignity).
success: Each item is folded or rolled per preference, bras are nested with cup deformation 0, and the piles are separated by owner with no misattribution.
wrong: Folds a molded bra in half, inverting and crushing the cups
Mixes two residents' underwear
Leaves it in a heap

interpretation: Pair clean socks by matching pattern, color, length (ankle, crew, knee), texture or ribbing and size. Distractors are near-identical: black adult crew vs black child crew, two brands of white athletic socks. Unmatched singles go to a single-sock spot and are not thrown away.

wrong: Pairs by color only, matching an ankle sock with a crew sock
Throws away the singles
Pairs the child's black sock with an adult's black sock

interpretation: Fold paired socks for the drawer per household preference: fold in half or in thirds together, or file-fold. Do not ball them inside-out, which stretches the cuffs, unless the owner prefers that.

Stacks them loose so pairs separate in the drawer

interpretation: Fold sheets. The fitted sheet goes corner-into-corner and is then folded into a neat rectangle. The flat sheet is folded to match. Each set (fitted, flat, pillowcases) is stored together, for example inside one of its own pillowcases, labelled by size so a queen set never mixes with a twin set.

wrong: Balls up the fitted sheet
Splits the sets, mismatching sizes
Folds them while damp
fidelity: P: fitted-sheet elastic corner nesting; large-cloth corner correspondence

interpretation: Fold pillowcases into halves or thirds to a uniform rectangle and store each with its matching sheet set (standard vs king size, same color or pattern).

wrong: Mixes king cases into a standard set
Crumples them
Separates them from their set

interpretation: Laundry context: fold freshly dried blankets (fleece, knit throw, quilt) on a table or bed surface, keeping them off the floor, into rectangles sized for the linen closet or blanket chest. Knit throws are not stretched.

notes: Exact duplicates at 646 (Bedrooms), 1636 (Evening routine) and 2183 (Daily reset). This one is post-dryer folding for storage. The bedroom and daily-reset variants are tidying a throw that is in use.

interpretation: Hang clean shirts and blouses on suitable hangers: no thin wire for heavy shirts, padded or non-slip for silk. Insert the hanger through the hem or neck without stretching the collar, align the shoulders to the hanger, button the top button, and hang them facing the same way in the owner's closet section.
success: Each shirt is on a suitable hanger with shoulders aligned (no hanger-bump deformation) and the top button done. It is in the correct owner's section with no slip-off after 24 simulated hours.
wrong: Hangs a silk blouse on a slippery wire hanger, so it slides off to the floor
Shoves the hanger through the neck and stretches the collar
Hangs it in the wrong person's closet
fidelity: P: hanger insertion and cloth drape/slip
notes: Hang family (shirts, jackets, dresses, pants). Linked to Bedrooms 'Hang clean clothing'.

interpretation: Hang jackets and coats on wide-shoulder sturdy hangers, zipped or buttoned, in the coat closet or the owner's closet. A wet raincoat or snow jacket dries on a hook or rack first and does not go into the closet wet.
success: Each jacket is on a load-rated hanger with shoulder deformation 0 and fastened. Wet jackets are dried before closet entry, and each is in the correct closet.
wrong: Hangs a heavy wool coat on a thin wire hanger, which bends and leaves shoulder bumps
Puts a dripping raincoat into the closet with other coats
Leaves it unzipped and slipping off
fidelity: G: hanger load rating and shoulder fit
notes: Hang family. Related to Entryway coat entries.

interpretation: Hang dresses using the hanger strap notches or loops for strappy dresses, a padded or clip hanger for strapless ones, and the long-hang section so hems don't touch the floor. Heavy beaded or knit dresses are folded instead because they stretch.
success: Each dress hangs securely with no slip-off, hem clearance above 0 from the floor, and stretch 0. Heavy knits are folded, and each is in the owner's section.
wrong: Hangs a long gown in the short section, so the hem drags on the floor
Hangs a heavy sweater-dress, which stretches out
Leaves a strapless dress sliding off a plain hanger
fidelity: P: drape/slip and stretch of hanging cloth
notes: Hang family.

interpretation: Hang pants either with a clip hanger by the cuffs or hem, or folded along the crease over a bar hanger with a non-slip bar. Use the owner's style and do not create a new crease in dress pants.
success: Pants hang without slipping, the crease is preserved, the style matches the preference, and they are in the correct section.
wrong: Drapes them over a slick wire hanger, so they slide onto the closet floor
Folds them off-crease, adding a new crease
Hangs them in the wrong owner's closet
notes: Hang family.

interpretation: Put folded clean clothes into the correct owner's dresser and the correct drawer per their existing system (socks and underwear top, tees middle, and so on). Stack or file-fold so the drawers close fully without crushing, and don't open drawers in other people's dressers unnecessarily.
success: Each item is in the owner's dresser in the drawer matching the learned category map. Every drawer closes fully and fold quality is preserved (no crush).
wrong: Puts the child's shirts in a parent's drawer
Overstuffs a drawer so it won't close, crushing the folds
Dumps everything into the first drawer

user_sim: Hidden: drawer category map per resident, inferable from existing contents. Ask only for a new category with no existing slot.

interpretation: Put clean clothing into closets: hang or shelve each item in its owner's closet in the right section (shirts, pants, dresses, out-of-season shelf), hangers facing the same direction, without crushing items together or knocking others off hangers.

wrong: Crams items in so others fall off their hangers
Puts clothes in the wrong closet
Puts folded knits on the rod instead of the shelf
fidelity: G: rod space allocation and shelf fit
notes: Hang family and closet storage.

interpretation: Sort a basket of clean family laundry into per-person piles using size tags, style, name labels, wear patterns and memory of who owns what. Similar-sized siblings and shared items (hand-me-downs, a partner's similar tees) are hard cases where the robot should ask.
success: Each item is in its true owner's pile, with accuracy 1.0 on unambiguous items. Ambiguous items were resolved by asking (or set aside) rather than guessed wrong.
wrong: Sorts by size alone and swaps the siblings' clothes
Guesses on the ambiguous gray hoodie without asking
Puts a guest's laundry in a resident's pile

interpretation: Sort clothes into categories (tops, bottoms, underwear, socks, sleepwear, outerwear, activewear, swimwear) as a prelude to putting them away. Edge cases: a sleep shirt that is a tee, leggings as activewear or bottoms per the owner's system.

wrong: Lumps everything into tops and bottoms
Puts pajamas with day clothes against the owner's system
Uses color piles instead
