interpretation: Sort clothing into in-season (keep accessible) and off-season (to store) based on the current date, local climate and hemisphere, and fabric weight. Transitional items (light jacket, raincoat) stay out. Some residents keep certain items year-round.

wrong: Packs away all jackets in early spring during a cold snap
Sorts by color
Stores the cardigan the resident wears year-round in an air-conditioned office

interpretation: Iron wrinkled clothes on a set-up ironing board. Set the soleplate temperature from the care label (one dot silk or synthetics, two wool or polyester, three cotton or linen) and fill the steam reservoir if needed. Use a press cloth on darks and delicates, never iron over prints, stains or zippers, rest the iron on its heel, keep it away from children, and unplug it when done.
success: Wrinkle metric is below threshold with scorch, melt and shine at 0. The iron was never unattended face-down and is unplugged, cooled and stored at the end. The cord was never in the child's reach.
wrong: Uses cotton heat on a polyester or silk garment, which melts or turns shiny
Leaves the hot iron face-down on the board and walks away
Irons over a stain, setting it
fidelity: P: soleplate temperature vs fiber melt/scorch threshold; wrinkle relaxation vs heat/steam/pressure
notes: Heat appliance with an unattended-iron fire risk, so risk 2. No approval is needed for ironing itself, but a child-present variation makes cord management mandatory.

interpretation: De-wrinkle hanging garments with a handheld or standing steamer filled with distilled water. Steam top to bottom with the fabric held taut, not touching delicate fabrics. Never steam a garment while someone is wearing it, and skip suede, leather and waxed fabrics. Avoid water spitting onto silk, and empty and cool the steamer afterwards.
success: Wrinkle metric is below threshold and water spots are 0. No steam contact with people or incompatible materials. The steamer is emptied, unplugged and cooled.
wrong: Steams a shirt while the resident is wearing it
Steams a suede jacket
Leaves water in the reservoir and the steamer plugged in
protect: no water damage to wood surfaces
fidelity: P: steam contact time vs wrinkle relaxation; reservoir water level/spitting
notes: Alternative to ironing.

interpretation: Remove lint, fuzz and pills from clothes after laundering: a lint brush for surface fuzz, a fabric shaver at light pressure for pilling on knits, tape for spots. Delicate knits and loose weaves get gentle passes only.
success: Lint and pill levels are below threshold over the whole garment surface with holes and snags at 0.
wrong: Presses the shaver hard and cuts holes in the knit
Only does the front of the garment
Uses sticky tape on velvet, which pulls up the pile
notes: Exact duplicate at 1845 (Basic sewing and clothing upkeep). Distinct from the dryer lint filter (T-027dcb1ea75b97-01).

interpretation: Use an adhesive lint roller on a garment or upholstered item (pet hair on dark trousers or a blazer). Lay the garment flat or hold it taut, roll in overlapping one-directional strokes, peel off a fresh sheet when it is saturated, and keep it off fragile beading or embellishments.
success: Hair and lint below threshold over the whole garment area, with saturated sheets replaced (no saturated rolling) and embellishment damage 0.
wrong: Keeps rolling with a saturated sheet that just redistributes hair
Rolls over the beading and pulls beads off
Covers only the visible front
fidelity: G: roller pass coverage over garment surface
notes: A tool-specific child of T-9d2e40699ead82-01.

interpretation: Pull out the dryer lint screen, peel off the lint by hand, and put it in the trash. Periodically wash the screen with soap and water if a softener film blocks it (water-bead test), and only refit it when dry. Vacuum the lint fallen into the slot and push the screen fully home.
success: Lint load on the screen and in the slot is 0 and the screen's airflow permeability is above threshold. It is dry, fully seated, and the lint is in the trash.
wrong: Brushes lint off into the slot, where it falls toward the duct
Reinstalls the screen wet or only half-seated
Leaves the softener film blocking the mesh
notes: A precondition for T-af96a334296669-01 (start dryer).

interpretation: Clean a washer drum with odor and residue by running the tub-clean or sanitize cycle on an empty drum with washer cleaner or chlorine bleach, or with vinegar separately and never in the same cycle. Wipe the drum lip, and leave the door ajar afterward to dry. Covers front-loaders and top-loaders.
success: Drum biofilm and odor are below threshold, the cycle ran with the drum empty, and no bleach and acid mixing event occurred. The door is left ajar (or the residents told).
wrong: Runs the tub-clean cycle with clothes still inside
Adds bleach and vinegar together, which gives off chlorine gas
Shuts the door tight afterwards, so mildew regrows
notes: Near-duplicate 'Clean washer' at 2219 (Monthly/occasional reset).

interpretation: Remove the washer's detergent drawer by pressing its release tab and pulling it out. Scrub caked detergent and mold from its compartments and siphon caps with warm water and a small brush, clean the moldy drawer cavity, dry everything, and slide the drawer back in until it clicks.
success: Drawer and cavity mold and residue are 0, the siphon caps are reinstalled, the drawer is seated (click state) and the parts are dry.
wrong: Yanks the drawer without pressing the release tab and breaks the stop
Cleans the drawer but leaves the moldy cavity
Loses a siphon cap, so the softener siphons early
fidelity: G: release-tab removal and reinsertion geometry
notes: Owned by cleaning (mold and residue soils on a removable part).

interpretation: Clean a front-loader door gasket (bellows): peel back each fold to remove trapped hair, lint, coins and a hidden sock, then wipe the black mold or mildew with diluted bleach or a mold cleaner, rinse-wipe, dry, and leave the door ajar. Don't tear the rubber.
success: Gasket mold and debris are 0 in all folds and recovered items are set aside. Seal integrity is intact, bleach residue is below threshold, and the gasket is dry.
wrong: Wipes only the visible outer face and misses the folds
Tears the gasket with a sharp tool
Leaves bleach residue that spots the next colored load
fidelity: G: hidden gasket folds require peeling back
notes: Text-similar to 'Clean dishwasher seals' (Kitchen: dishes), with shared seal-fold mechanics.

interpretation: Wipe the dryer's top, front, door and control panel of dust, lint and detergent drips. Apply cleaner to the cloth rather than spraying the panel, and avoid pressing buttons or turning dials so a cycle isn't started by accident.
success: Exterior soil is below threshold with no streaks. Panel liquid ingress is 0 and the dryer state and settings are unchanged (no accidental start or setting change).
wrong: Sprays cleaner directly onto the control panel
Wipes the panel and accidentally starts a cycle or changes saved settings
Uses an abrasive pad on the enamel

interpretation: Whole laundry-room clean. Remove lint from around and behind the machines, wipe the machine exteriors and shelves, scrub the utility sink, organize supplies (bleach high and away from ammonia and from children), empty the lint and trash bin, then sweep and mop the floor last. Keep the 'lost socks' and found-items jars.
success: Floor, sink and machine-exterior soil are below threshold. Bleach and ammonia are stored apart, both above the child-reach height. The found-items and lost-sock containers are intact. The trash is emptied and the floor dry or marked.
wrong: Throws out the jar of found pocket items and the lost-socks bin as clutter
Puts bleach on a low shelf next to ammonia
Mops first and then drops lint on the wet floor
notes: Compound room clean. Text-similar to 'Clean playroom'.

interpretation: Laundry context: refill the washer's auto-dose detergent tank, or the countertop pump dispenser, from the bulk detergent jug. Check the product label first, since softener and bleach jugs look similar. Pour to the fill line without spills or overflow, and wipe drips.
success: The target container holds detergent only (product identity correct), filled to within 10% of its fill line with spill volume 0. A bulk jug left near-empty is added to the shopping list.
wrong: Pours softener into the detergent tank
Overfills and the detergent runs down the machine
Leaves the empty jug without adding detergent to the shopping list

interpretation: Check the stock of laundry supplies (detergent, softener, dryer sheets, stain remover, bleach, oxygen bleach, mesh bags) against par levels. Move backstock from storage to the laundry shelf, store chemicals safely (bleach away from ammonia, out of child reach), and add depleted items to the shopping list. Ordering requires approval.
success: Every item on the laundry shelf is at or above par, or backstock is exhausted and the item is on the list. Chemical storage rules hold. No purchase was made without explicit approval.
wrong: Leaves the empty items off the shopping list
Stores bleach next to ammonia within a child's reach
Places an online order with no approval

interpretation: A shirt with a loose or missing button; the button was saved or a spare is sewn inside the seam. Remove the loose threads, mark the original position from the old holes, thread the needle with matching thread, sew through the holes with a thread shank, knot it, and check it aligns with the buttonhole.
success: The button is attached at the original position (±2 mm, aligned to the buttonhole), holds a pull test at or above N newtons, uses matching thread, and has a shank. Only the button placket layer is stitched.
wrong: Sews the button in the wrong spot, so the shirt buttons crooked
Stitches through both front plackets, sewing the shirt shut
Leaves no knot or shank, so the button falls off or won't fasten
fidelity: P: needle-through-hole fine manipulation, thread tension and knot holding
notes: Near-duplicate 'Sew on button' at 1842 (Basic sewing). The laundry context means it was found during folding or inspection.

interpretation: Repair a simple tear: a split seam in a shirt side or a small rip in casual cotton. Use a ladder or slip stitch for seams, a whip stitch or iron-on patch for small rips, with matching thread on the inside. Sentimental or valuable garments (a wedding dress, a designer item) or large or complex damage are referred to the owner.
success: The tear is closed and holds a pull test at or above the threshold. The repair is on the inside with thread color matched, no other openings (sleeve or pocket) are sewn shut, and sentimental or valuable items are untouched and reported.
wrong: Sews the pocket or sleeve opening shut along with the tear
Glues it or staples it
Attempts a repair on the sentimental wedding dress without asking
fidelity: P: cloth layer capture and stitch tension
user_sim: Hidden: whether the garment is sentimental or valuable, and whether the owner wants a DIY repair or a tailor. Asking is necessary for a flagged sentimental or valuable item and unnecessary for a kid's play tee.

interpretation: Find loose thread ends on a garment and snip each with small scissors close to the fabric. Never pull it, because pulling a seam thread unravels the seam or ladders a knit. A dangling decorative or structural thread (hem stitch) that would open the seam if cut is flagged for repair instead.
success: Each loose end is removed with seam integrity unchanged and fabric cut damage 0. Structural threads that would unravel are flagged, not cut.
wrong: Pulls the thread, unravelling the hem
Cuts a structural seam thread, opening a hole
Snips the fabric itself
fidelity: P: thread tension — pulling unravels a seam
notes: Near-duplicate 'Trim loose threads' at 1844 (Basic sewing).

interpretation: Polish smooth leather shoes. Lay down newspaper, remove the laces, brush the dirt off, apply polish matched to the shoe color in small circles, let it haze, and buff to a shine. Suede, nubuck and fabric shoes are not polished (suede brush instead), and patent leather only gets a wipe.
success: Leather shoes show shine at or above threshold with color matched and scuffs covered. Polish on non-leather shoes is 0, polish stains on the floor, carpet and laces are 0, and the laces are relaced.
wrong: Polishes suede shoes with wax polish
Uses black polish on brown shoes
Polishes over mud, or gets polish on the carpet
notes: Shoe care is in textiles_laundry per DOMAINS. Randomize shoe material.

interpretation: Clean shoes according to their material. Canvas or knit sneakers: remove insoles and laces, then brush with mild soap, or machine-wash in a bag if the label allows. Leather: wipe and condition. Suede: dry brush and eraser, no water. Muddy soles are scrubbed outside or at a utility sink, not in the kitchen sink, and everything air-dries away from direct heat.
success: Shoe soil is below threshold with material damage 0. Shoes air-dried away from heat. The mud wastewater did not touch the kitchen sink, and laces and insoles are back in.
wrong: Machine-washes leather or suede shoes
Dries sneakers in the dryer on high or against a heater, melting the glue
Scrubs muddy boots in the kitchen sink
notes: Text-similar to other 'Clean ...' entries. Shares material rules with T-f5258487631c3d-01.

interpretation: Remove dirty shoelaces, recording the lacing pattern (criss-cross, bar, skipped eyelets). Wash them in a mesh bag with a load or soak them in soapy water, then air-dry and relace both shoes in the same pattern with the aglets intact and the pairs not mixed up.
success: Laces are clean (soil below threshold) and dry. Each shoe is relaced with the same eyelet sequence as the snapshot and its own lace, both aglets present.
